data.description:
## Why
Installed skill copies go stale, and an agent then follows commands the running app does not have. The copy inside the app bundle matches that build. There is no way to print it, and `capabilities` is a method list with no feature flags, so a skill cannot tell what this build actually supports. Backlog item: C6.

## Evidence
- c11: `CLI/c11.swift` has no `guide`, `--skill`, or `rpc` case on origin/main (0ff8887e5e). `git grep` for those command names in the CLI is empty. `c11 skill` manages installed copies (`skills/c11/references/api.md:409-425`) and does not print the skill text.
- c11: `Sources/SocketHandlers/SystemHandlers.swift:53-120` (`v2Capabilities`) returns a hand-kept `methods` array. There is no `features` list and no build identity in that payload. The CLI `capabilities` case (`CLI/c11.swift`, the `case "capabilities"` next to `ping`) connects to the socket before it can print anything.
- c11: `CLAUDE.md` states the install is a one-time copy into `~/.claude/skills/<name>/`, and `scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh` is the refresh. A printed guide does not replace that sync.
- Upstream: cmux #12468 prints `guide` and `--skill` before the CLI looks for a socket. cmux #16460 shows a hand-kept capabilities list drifting from dispatch. `rpc` is the other half of report 06 §1i and is backlog C7, not this ticket.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` §1i. `c11-1.0.html` marks `c11 guide` and the feature flags core, and marks `c11 rpc` if-time. Fable bundled guide and rpc as one row. The backlog splits them. Astra row 4.9: print CLI build identity and guide version, and compare server identity when a socket is connected. A PATH binary can differ from the app.

## Scope
In: `c11 guide` and `c11 --skill` print the c11 skill bundled in the same build as the CLI, with no socket required. The output includes the CLI's build identity (version and a git sha or build stamp the binary already has). When a socket connects, also print or JSON-encode the server identity from `system.capabilities` or `system.brand` so a mismatch is visible. Add a versioned `features` array on `system.capabilities`, generated from the same table as `methods` or from a small explicit registry next to dispatch, not a second hand-kept list that can drift. Seed it with flags for behavior already on origin/main that skills branch on, and leave named slots for C1 (`routing.canonical_keys`), C2 (`create.initial_input`), C3 (`send.raw`), C4 (`read_selection.terminal`), and C5 (`window.route_without_focus`). Those slots appear only when the behavior is in the build.
Out: `c11 rpc` (C7). `config doctor` (parked, report 06 §1j). Parameter schemas for every method (report 06 defers that to the 1.x registry). Rewriting the installed skill, or auto-syncing it on launch. The summonable fork-walkthrough agent (C11-104's area). That is a different product.

## Approach
Ship the skill markdown in the app bundle next to the CLI, or read it from the bundle's `Resources` if it is already copied there. `guide` and `--skill` run before `SocketClient.connect`. Exit 0 even when no app is running. `features` is an array of `{id, version}` or strings plus a `features_version` integer. Bump `features_version` when a flag's meaning changes. Add a test that every `features` id is also mentioned by the dispatch or by a registry the dispatch reads, so a stale string fails in `c11-logic`. Document `c11 guide` in the skill itself, including the line that an installed copy can be older than `c11 guide`. Do not have `guide` write `~/.claude/skills`.

## Acceptance criteria
1. With no c11 app running, `c11 guide` prints the skill markdown and a build identity, and exits 0. `c11 --skill` prints the same body.
2. The printed text includes a command that exists in this CLI and does not include a command the CLI help rejects. Check one added command and one removed one against `c11 --help`.
3. Against a running tagged build, `c11 capabilities --json` includes `features` and a server identity. If the CLI sha and the server sha differ, the JSON says so rather than printing only the CLI's copy.
4. A unit test fails if a feature id is added to the capabilities payload without a registry entry the dispatch table shares. Run it on `c11-logic`.
5. `c11 guide` does not create or modify `~/.claude/skills/c11`. Confirm with mtime before and after.

## Validation
`c11-logic` for the registry test. A `tests_v2` or CLI smoke against a tagged build for criteria 1 through 3 and 5. No computer-use pass. No soak. Guide is offline. Capabilities is one socket call.

## Dependencies
None required to start. C1, C2, C3, C4, and C5 register the flag names above when they land. If this ticket lands first, the array exists and those tickets add their ids. If one of them lands first, it adds the id in the same shape this ticket specifies, or leaves a one-line note in its PR. Do not block those tickets on this one.

## Risks
Typing latency: none. Main thread: `system.capabilities` is a snapshot. Keep the handler as it is. Do not rebuild the method list by walking live windows. Doctrine: printing the bundled skill is not a tenant-config write. The sync script remains the way an installed copy updates. Localization: `guide` prints the English skill source. Do not run it through the six-locale catalog. Public repo: the skill is already public.

Size: S–M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: the running build tells the truth about itself. It does not rewrite the operator's skill install.

CI run https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/actions/runs/36965654274 at c2a7da2c1ee8a089496693aa9b5d0f7ca6f08130 compiled the app and tests. The offline guide checks again passed, as did the five helper/identity tests and both registry tests. The synthetic peer then closed immediately after sending the capability response. The existing SocketClient.send read loop sets SO_RCVTIMEO again after seeing a newline; the disconnected peer made that setsockopt fail. The harness now models c11's persistent socket contract by keeping the peer alive until the client disconnects, without touching the production transport.

The same run also timed out in the unchanged WorkspaceRemoteConnectionTests.testRemoteRelayMetadataCleanupScriptPreservesDifferentSocketAddr at line 122. No changes to that test, its implementation or its skip policy are made here. The first run passed it. This is a separate baseline timeout, not tagged runtime proof or a C11-284 feature defect.

# C11-284 review, cycle 1

Verdict: FAIL at 0e83c435cd40a7f53c43cf22ef070e34303b3727.
Base: 0ff8887e5e965400b01645ef40b85fd0b2605cf2 (merge-base with refreshed origin/main).

## Blocking

1. **CLI/c11.swift:1867: plain guide connects during discovery before its offline return.** From an ordinary shell with no socket environment override and no explicit --socket, `c11 guide` calls CLISocketPathResolver.resolve at line 1776 before reaching this new branch. The implicit-default resolver calls canConnect for discovered socket candidates (lines 866-870), which calls Darwin.connect (line 995). If a discoverable c11 listener exists, printing the guide opens and closes a real connection to it. `c11 --skill` returns before this discovery, so the two advertised offline forms differ. This violates the new guide help/skill promise of printing without connecting to a socket and the plan's offline-guide contract. The smoke at tests_v2/test_guide_and_features.py:44-47 always supplies --socket, which bypasses that resolver branch and cannot detect it. Smallest fix: handle guide, including its help, before socket resolution; leave the other command paths alone. Add a built-CLI scenario with socket overrides cleared and a discoverable fixture listener: guide and --skill must print identical bodies without the listener accepting any connection. This is a static call-path finding; no runtime reproduction was performed here.

## Non-blocking

1. **tests_v2/test_guide_and_features.py:53:** the removed-command check runs `list` against a nonexistent socket. Any socket-dependent command would fail before dispatch in that setup, so this does not establish that list is rejected as unknown. The current dispatch does omit list, so this is a coverage weakness rather than another product defect. In the tagged smoke, check its unknown-command error against the test server, retaining the no-app guide checks separately.

## Review coverage

Read the ticket, stored plan, validation event ev_01M3XG0DF39M0N6AE80DJ8FCK5, project policies, philosophy, C11-188 AAR, all ten changed files, and the affected executable resolution, socket discovery, dispatch, identity formatting, bundle-copy and target-membership seams. The checkout is clean and the remote branch still equals the reviewed head.

The registry enables the three existing features and registers all five pending features disabled. It provides a shared admission/serialization seam for later owners; both app and CLI compile the helper. The fixture tests exercise disabled/missing admission, enabled execution, bundle loading and build identity. Bundle-only identity avoids checkout/environment fallbacks; capabilities adds CLI identity to the server response and handles unknown and prefix-matching stamps. The methods list, socket threading policy, focus prelude, send delivery and mailbox implementation are unchanged. Guide has no installed-skill write path. No additional blocking findings.

## Runtime proof still required

- After repair, obtain green exact-head CI, including CapabilityFeaturesTests, BundledSkillTests and the entire corrected bundled-CLI smoke. Prior-head passes and the queued run described by the owner are not exact-head success.
- Atlas/batch Validator must run tests_v2/test_guide_and_features.py --foundation-only against the tagged C11-284-only app and its bundled CLI: three existing ids present, five pending ids absent, feature versions and CLI/server identities correct, guide/alias/page/error behavior correct, installed skill unchanged. Include the implicit-discovery no-connection scenario above. The synthetic identity peer checks supplement, but do not replace, live-server proof.
- As subsequent feature PRs land, their behavior and enabled registry entries must land together. The integrated artifact must compare the five real feature scenarios with the advertised ids; the foundation-only absence check is not the integrated sign-off.

No builds, tests or app launches were performed in this review. The pending CI and live proof are assigned external gates by the review brief, not additional code-review blockers by themselves. The recorded scenario is useful but needs the missing default-discovery case before it proves the complete offline claim.

# C11-284 bundle identity diagnosis and runtime checks

Needs operator: nothing. Offline and live runtime PASS on the exact candidate. Nullable commit remains unknown; version/build supplies the permitted build stamp identity.

Candidate: merged head `b6f239bd077164d2ff2e7aa18d5464d4e885fd35`, canonical invocation `273d23384a7a436b8d5d14b81eb6f292`, clean source/empty overlay. Build-host executable SHA256 `4f964b60873ddb4dfae4153ea2e1308605ba0995480acb344e2614e3fc6524ac`; separately signed interactive-session/guest copy SHA256 `25be5130f86178e852a6da28b05966ab9c750bf48ab3c76a86c417d7807115fc`.

## Finding: pre-existing stamp phase can run too early

The build-host's actual current `$HOME`-owned tag build log (`/tmp/c11-xcodebuild-val-3.log`) places app `PhaseScriptExecution Run Script` at line 233, then app `ProcessInfoPlistFile` at line 810. The script stamps `${TARGET_BUILD_DIR}/${INFOPLIST_PATH}` only when the file already exists. Xcode subsequently generates the product Info.plist from `Resources/Info.plist`, which contains no C11Commit/CMUXCommit. Thus a fresh product can skip stamping, and an existing stamped product can be overwritten by the later plist task. The final packaged Info.plist indeed contains version `0.67.0`, build `131`, and neither commit key.

This is an actual packaging ordering weakness, not evidence that Debug intentionally never stamps. The existing stamp block has no Debug exemption. Git history places the C11Commit phase under earlier branding commit `6d0bc1a843` (#37), before C11-284. `scripts/reload.sh` retags/re-signs after xcodebuild and does not re-add C11Commit; the nightly workflow independently stamps both commit keys after building. No build, plist edit, new stamp, source change or signing change was performed for this diagnosis.

## Contract: nullable commit is represented honestly

C11-284's ticket explicitly accepts version plus git SHA **or build stamp**. `Sources/BundledSkill.swift:3` confines identity to the built bundle, models commit as optional, prints version/build even without a commit, and returns unknown (`nil`/JSON null) from commitsMatch when either commit is unavailable or malformed. CLI capabilities help at `CLI/c11.swift:8684` says sha_match is null when either build lacks a stamp. This runtime supports an unstamped bundle honestly; that fallback does not imply the packaging ordering weakness is desirable.

The stock `tests_v2/test_guide_and_features.py:83` imposes a stricter non-null commit assertion, then its synthetic-case construction calls `.startswith` on that assumed non-null value. That fixture rejects a permitted build-stamp identity. The ignored `C11-284-nullable-runtime.py` changes only the fixture assumptions: require version/build and its printed header; retain actual commit null; compare null/missing/valid/invalid/empty synthetic peer commits with the expected unknown result. It does not mint a fake stamp, edit the app, or replace shipping source.

## Observed execution

- Exact built CLI on the build host, offline: PASS. Plain guide/alias/help match with socket overrides cleared and a discoverable synthetic listener receiving no connection. Explicit dead socket guide, bundle source/version/body, command/reference/help, invalid/missing page errors and reachable-peer removed `list` rejection all pass. Installed skill mtime/size state unchanged.
- Five executable synthetic capability peers: server explicit null, server identity absent, valid `111111111`, malformed `invalid`, and empty commit all yield `sha_match:null` with the CLI's actual `commit:null`. No true/false SHA match is claimed from an unstamped CLI.
- Real isolated guest, ready-target retry: PASS, exit0. Re-signed executable SHA256 verified. A single read returned features_version1 and the three foundation IDs; CLI and server both reported `0.67.0`/`131`/null with matching bundle identifiers, and `sha_match:null`. Installed skill state remained unchanged. The earlier unavailable-socket attempt is retained as lifecycle evidence, not a product failure. No launch/recovery/mutation was performed for the live read.

Artifacts: `C11-284-nullable-runtime.py` (ignored adaptation), `C11-284-offline-public.log`, `C11-284-live-ready.log` (successful read), `C11-284-live-public.log` (failed attempt retained), and this report. All actual home paths are rendered as `$HOME`; no account/machine names, emails, provider session IDs or shell prompts appear in this report.

## Acceptance

PASS on the ticket's permitted version/build fallback, independently exercised offline and live. No git SHA match is claimed. The pre-existing stamping phase ordering weakness is disclosed separately; it does not invalidate the honestly nullable runtime contract. Parent records the verdict; no Lattice writes were performed.

Built-CLI offline guide/alias/help/discovery/error checks and five synthetic nullable comparisons passed. One real isolated-guest capabilities read passed with version0.67.0/build131, actual commitnull, sha_matchnull, the three enabled foundation features and unchanged installed skills. Version/build satisfies the ticket identity fallback. Pre-existing plist stamp phase ordering is disclosed; no fake stamp or source/app modification was made. Parent records the verdict.
